title: Navigators with feathers
text: Every autumn billions of birds undertake journeys that human navigators would struggle to {{1}}: crossings of deserts and open ocean, made without maps, lessons or visible landmarks. An Arctic tern's annual round trip of some 70,000 kilometres is extraordinary enough, but a bird displaced hundreds of kilometres off course can still {{2}} its bearings and set off again, which shows it is following not a memorised road but a genuine {{3}} of the world. To do this it reads the sun by day and the stars by night, and it also {{4}} the Earth's magnetic field — a signal so weak that a pocket compass would barely {{5}}. The most likely {{6}} is a quantum one: proteins in the retina whose behaviour changes with the field's {{7}}, letting the bird see a compass laid across its vision. Whatever the exact mechanism, the {{8}} is unambiguous: each autumn, without a single lesson, a billion tiny brains navigate the planet.

gaps.explanation: 'journeys that human navigators would struggle to match' — equal or rival; counter and undo respond to or reverse, and mend repairs.
'can still find its bearings' — work out its position; feign = pretend, fend takes 'for', forge = fake.
'a genuine representation of the world' — an inner model of it; the other nouns share the prefix but not the meaning.
'it also detects the Earth's magnetic field' — registers its presence; deter = discourage, detach = unfasten.
'a pocket compass would barely twitch' — give a tiny movement; switch = change, and needles twitch rather than pitch or stitch.
'the most likely explanation is a quantum one' — the best account; the other nouns share 'exp-' beginnings but differ completely.
'changes with the field's direction' — the way it runs; the compass metaphor points to orientation, not places or notices.
'the outcome is unambiguous' — the result; outlet = a means of release, output = production, outset = the beginning.
